newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle seen steady-up, feeders steady-off.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle seen steady-up, feeders steady-off.

text.p: CME live cattle futures were expected to open steady to 0.150 cent per lb higher while feeder cattle were called steady to 0.100 lower, livestock analysts said.

The rise in boxed beef values Tuesday came sooner than expected and this may prompt early support in live cattle futures. Beef prices turned up after falling to two week lows on Monday. Retailers are expected to build their cooler stocks for upcoming holidays in May, analysts said.
Cash cattle prices may also end up being firmer than expected, they said.
Although packers continued to bid $66 per cwt for fed cattle, expectations were that cash cattle may trade at $67 before the day is over based on the stronger boxed beef market, they said.
The discount of June to cash was also viewed as supportive, they added.

The drop in the latest CME index and higher corn futurs indications could weigh on feeder cattle futures initially. However, analysts looked for underlying support as the next moves in the index were expected to be up.

The decline in the index came from a larger than normal Texas direct trade and later auction sales were higher, including Oklahoma City which was steady to higher. The index should move higher in the next quote, they added.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.83 to $71.95 per cwt.
